issues.legal_issue: An appeal from an environmental tribunal’s decision is confined to substantial questions of law and does not permit a fresh assessment of the facts and evidence.
material_facts: The appeals challenged decisions of the environmental tribunal, and the appellants sought to contest findings based on the evidence and factual record.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the appeals could not be used to reappreciate the factual matrix or evidence; the statutory appeal was confined to substantial questions of law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 22 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 makes an appeal subject to the grounds in Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908. A substantial question of law is assessed by the test in Sir Chunilal V. Mehta and Sons, Ltd. v. Century Spinning and Manufacturing: it must be of general public importance or substantially affect the parties’ rights and be open, unsettled, difficult, or call for discussion of alternative views. A settled principle’s application to facts, or a request to reappraise evidence, is not enough.

predicates.appeal_from_environmental_tribunal: The proceeding is an appeal from a decision of a specialist environmental tribunal.
predicates.challenge_requires_reassessment_of_evide: The appellant’s challenge asks the appellate court to reassess the facts or evidence considered by the tribunal.

issues.definition: When an appeal from an environmental tribunal asks for reassessment of the tribunal’s factual record, the appellate court does not undertake that reassessment.

issues.legal_issue: An application seeking restoration of the environment falls within the tribunal’s independent restorative jurisdiction and is governed by its separate, longer limitation period rather than the limitation period for an ordinary environmental dispute application.
material_facts: The application sought restoration of ecologically sensitive land and the maintenance of its natural condition, relying on reports concerning the area’s environmental condition.
The record documented breaches by the project proponents and indicated that the projects could seriously affect the ecology, hydrology, and environment of the lake catchment area.
The application was filed in March 2014, after the cited reports in 2013.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the application was a restorative application, not merely an application under the ordinary environmental-dispute jurisdiction, and was not barred by time.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14 and 15 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 provide distinct and independent jurisdictions and limitation periods. Section 15(1)(b) and (c) authorizes restitution of damaged property and restoration of the environment, with Section 15(1)(c) read with Section 20 supporting preventive and restorative measures. Section 18 recognizes applications under both sections. The ordinary dispute limitation under Section 14(3) is distinct from the limitation under Section 15(3); the latter allows an application within five years of the cause for compensation or relief first arising. The Act is beneficial legislation and its restorative jurisdiction is to be interpreted broadly, as supported by Kishore Lal v. Chairman, Employees’ State Insurance Corpn.

predicates.restorative_environment_application: The applicant seeks restoration of the environment or of property damaged by environmental harm.
predicates.documented_environmental_degradation: Reports or other record material document environmental degradation or a serious environmental threat connected to the challenged activity.
predicates.filed_within_applicable_restoration_limi: The application was filed within the limitation period applicable to a claim for environmental restoration.

issues.definition: A timely application seeking environmental restoration, supported by material documenting degradation or a serious threat, is entertainable as a restorative application.

issues.legal_issue: The tribunal’s restorative environmental jurisdiction can support buffer-zone directions even when those directions conflict with inconsistent state planning laws or planning instruments.
material_facts: The state and other appellants argued that the tribunal’s enlarged buffer zones conflicted with the statutory master plan and other state planning laws.
The applicants argued that the tribunal’s environmental-restoration powers prevailed over inconsistent planning requirements.
The Supreme Court held that the tribunal’s restorative powers could support buffer zones contrary to inconsistent zoning regulations.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court held that the tribunal could specify buffer zones for environmental restoration notwithstanding inconsistent state planning laws or planning regulations. It later set aside the general buffer-zone direction for the other appellants, except insofar as it applied to the project proponents, because the applicants did not object to that relief.
issues.legal_principle: Section 33 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 gives the Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws and instruments having effect by virtue of law. Read with Sections 15(1)(c) and 20, that authority permits the tribunal to prescribe environmental-restoration measures, including buffer zones, despite inconsistent state zoning rules. The Court also relied on the overriding effect of central legislation enacted under Entry 13 of List I of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.

predicates.environmental_restoration_proceeding: The proceeding asks the tribunal to take measures to restore or protect the environment.
predicates.restorative_buffer_measure_needed: The tribunal considers a buffer zone necessary as an environmental-restoration measure.
predicates.buffer_conflicts_with_state_zoning: The proposed buffer zone differs from a buffer or zoning requirement in a state planning law or instrument.

issues.definition: When a restoration proceeding calls for a buffer zone that conflicts with state zoning, the tribunal may prescribe the buffer as a restorative measure, subject to the scope of the appeals and relief sought.

issues.legal_issue: Environmental directions and compensation imposed on project proponents may be sustained where supported by the evidentiary record of breaches and environmental harm, and the appellate court cannot revisit those findings through factual reappraisal.
material_facts: The tribunal found that construction had begun before environmental clearance, that drains had been encroached upon or affected, and that project conditions protecting natural drainage, hydrology, and water bodies had been breached.
The tribunal’s findings relied on documentary material, satellite images, committee reports, and expert inspection material.

The tribunal found that the project proponents continued their activities despite being unable to comply with environmental-clearance conditions and imposed environmental compensation and restorative directions.
The Supreme Court found the tribunal’s conclusions supported by the record and found no perversity in its directions or compensation orders.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court dismissed the project proponents’ appeals and sustained the tribunal’s directions and environmental compensation against them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the environmental-clearance requirements in the Environment Impact Assessment Notification, 2006, and the environmental principles of sustainable development, precaution, and polluter pays. Under Section 22 of the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010, an appeal does not permit factual reappraisal. The Court held that the tribunal’s findings, based on the record and expert material, were not perverse and that its directions and compensation were sustainable.

predicates.appeal_by_project_proponent_from_environ: The proceeding is an appeal by a project proponent challenging an environmental tribunal’s order.
predicates.recorded_environmental_breaches: The tribunal found that the project proponent breached environmental requirements or conditions attached to its approvals.
predicates.evidence_supports_adverse_environmental_: Documents, reports, images, or expert inspection material support the tribunal’s findings of actual or potential environmental harm.
predicates.continued_activity_despite_clearance_con: The project proponent continued project activity despite conditions protecting the environment that it could not comply with.

issues.definition: Where a project proponent appeals an environmental order, supported findings of breaches and environmental harm, together with continued activity despite protective conditions, support sustaining the tribunal’s directions and compensation.

issues.legal_issue: Parallel proceedings do not bar an environmental application by res judicata or constructive res judicata when the parties, causes of action, and matters directly and substantially in issue are not materially the same.
material_facts: Related writ petitions were pending before a High Court while the environmental application was before the tribunal.

The tribunal found that the parties and causes of action were different, that the writ petitions concerned land acquisition, allotment, and transfer, and that the tribunal application concerned environmental effects and restoration.
The tribunal found no substantial identity between the matters in issue and no material likelihood of conflicting judgments.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court upheld the tribunal’s finding that the environmental application was not barred by res judicata or constructive res judicata.
issues.legal_principle: The doctrine of res judicata and its constructive form require material identity in the parties and in the matters directly and substantially in issue; they serve finality and prevent repeated litigation. The Court accepted the tribunal’s findings that the proceedings had distinct causes of action, issues, scope, and relief.

rule.if: environmental_application and parallel_proceeding_exists and (parties_are_materially_different or causes_of_action_are_distinct or issues_are_not_substantially_identical)

predicates.environmental_application: The proceeding seeks relief concerning environmental effects or environmental restoration.
predicates.parallel_proceeding_exists: Another judicial proceeding involving related events or property is pending or has been brought.
predicates.parties_are_materially_different: The parties to the two proceedings are not materially the same.
predicates.causes_of_action_are_distinct: The proceedings arise from different causes of action.
predicates.issues_are_not_substantially_identical: The matters directly and substantially in issue in the proceedings are not materially the same.

issues.definition: A related parallel proceeding does not bar an environmental application when the parties, causes of action, or issues are materially distinct.

issues.legal_issue: A general buffer-zone direction extending beyond the project proponents in the original environmental proceeding may be set aside for other appellants who were not parties before the tribunal when the applicants do not oppose that relief.
material_facts: Several appellants had not been parties before the tribunal and challenged a general direction prescribing buffer zones for water bodies and drains.

The applicants stated that the applications before the tribunal had been brought only against the two project proponents and did not object to setting aside the general direction for the other appellants.
The Supreme Court set aside the general direction for the other appellants while preserving the directions against the project proponents.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court allowed the other appeals and set aside the general buffer-zone direction insofar as it applied to those appellants, while leaving the direction against the project proponents in force.
issues.legal_principle: The Court gave effect to the applicants’ position that the original environmental applications were directed only against the project proponents. Because the applicants did not oppose setting aside the general direction for the other appellants, the Court quashed that portion while preserving the project-specific directions.

predicates.appeal_from_general_environmental_direct: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a general environmental direction.
predicates.appellant_was_not_party_to_original_proc: The appellant was not a party to the original proceeding in which the direction was made.
predicates.direction_applies_beyond_original_projec: The direction extends to persons or projects beyond those originally proceeded against.
predicates.applicants_do_not_oppose_setting_it_asid: The applicants in the original proceeding do not oppose setting aside the direction for the appellant.

issues.definition: A general environmental direction is set aside for a non-party appellant when it extends beyond the original project proponents and the applicants do not oppose that relief.
